title: Sesame hardware map (F4 boundary inventory)
description: Machine-readable inventory of every hardware and I/O boundary in the Sesame robot firmware, extracted from pinned source with file:line provenance. Strict throughout: additionalProperties is false on every object, so a typo'd or undocumented key is a hard failure rather than a silent gap. Every fact-bearing object carries a `source` (or `<fact>Source`) pointer; a fact without provenance is a bug.

boards.description: Every pin configuration present in source, active and commented-out alike.
boards.$comment: Exactly one board must be active; enforced below.

unresolved.description: Every fact that could not be established from source. Missing/ambiguous data is null in place AND listed here with a reason. Never invented.

source.description: Provenance pointer. `file` is relative to the UPSTREAM repository root (e.g. "firmware/sesame-firmware-main.ino"), not to this repository.

librarySource.description: Provenance for a fact that comes from a third-party Arduino LIBRARY rather than from Sesame's own firmware. The library tree is installed under the gitignored tools/ directory, so a repo path would not survive a clean clone; the citable identity is library + version + path-within-the-library + line. Deliberately NOT the two-key {file,line} shape, so scripts/validate-hardware-map.mjs --check-lines does not try to resolve it against the firmware tree.

file.description: Path relative to the library root, e.g. "src/ESP32Servo.h".

text.description: What is actually at that line, so a reader can confirm a match after a version bump.

versionPin.description: Where the version is pinned, e.g. reproducibility.json -> libraries.ESP32Servo.

active.description: True for the configuration that is uncommented in the checked-in source.

servoPins.description: ORDERED by firmware servo index (R1,R2,L1,L2,R4,R3,L3,L4), not by GPIO number.

then.$comment: An unverified claim must say where it came from.

order.description: The firmware enum order, pinned as a const so it can never be silently re-sorted. It is deliberately NOT geometric and NOT alphabetical.

attachMinPulseUs.description: EFFECTIVE minimum pulse, after the library's own clamp. See attachPulseClamp.

attachMaxPulseUs.description: EFFECTIVE maximum pulse, after the library's own clamp — the number every angle-to-pulse calculation must use. The value the firmware ASKED for is attachMaxPulseRequestedUs. See attachPulseClamp.

attachMaxPulseRequestedUs.description: What sesame-firmware-main.ino:742 passes to attach(). Kept alongside the effective value because both are true and a reader must be able to see why they differ.

positionFeedback.description: Structurally pinned to null: the stock robot has no joint-position feedback. If this ever becomes non-null the schema must change deliberately.

bootBlocker.description: True when a failure at this boundary prevents setup() from completing.

bootFailureCode.description: Verbatim quote of the failure path from source.

method.description: The method the route is REGISTERED for. WebServer::on(uri, handler) binds HTTP_ANY; per-handler restrictions are recorded in methodEnforcedInHandler.

loops.description: True when loop() will re-invoke the function because it does not clear currentCommand.

interruptible.description: True when the function contains pressingCheck() interrupt points.

step.description: One statement of choreography. Control flow is represented structurally (repeat/conditional carry nested step lists) rather than flattened, except where a literal-bound loop expands exactly — those steps carry `expandedFrom`.

expandedFrom.description: Present when this step came from exactly expanding a literal-bound loop.

count.description: Literal iteration count, or null when the bound is a runtime variable named by countRef.

then.$comment: A repeat must be bounded by either a literal count or a named runtime variable — never neither.

frameCount.description: Frames countFrames() will actually find at runtime — 0 when the base bitmap symbol is an unresolved weak reference.

orphanFrameSymbols.description: Frame bitmaps that are defined in source but unreachable, because an earlier frame index is missing and countFrames() stops at the first null.

playbackModes.description: Modes actually observed at setFaceWithMode() call sites. Empty means the face has no intrinsic mode — see faces.playbackModeOwnership.

then.$comment: A zero-frame face must explain itself; silence would look like a transcription error.

bootStep.description: One ordered operation in setup(). This array IS the R4 milestone ladder, so its order must match the source exactly.

bootBlocker.description: True only when source demonstrably prevents setup() from completing on failure (e.g. an infinite loop), not merely when failure is likely.

subject.description: Dotted path into this document that the entry qualifies.

value.description: The value recorded in the document — null when nothing could be established, or the best-known value when it is recorded but unverified.
